title: Somali National Army Joins Multinational Military Exercise in Turkey, Deepening Ankara-Mogadishu Defense Partnership
detail: The Somali National Army participated in a multinational military exercise hosted by Turkey on May 2, 2026, in a demonstration of the deepening bilateral defense partnership between Ankara and Mogadishu. Turkey has been Somalia's most consistent bilateral defense partner since President Erdogan's 2011 Mogadishu visit during the famine, and currently operates Camp Turksom — Turkey's largest overseas military base — near Mogadishu, which has trained over 10,000 SNA soldiers. The May 2 exercise comes as Turkey has dramatically expanded its economic footprint in Somalia in 2026: Turkish drillship Çağrı Bey began Somalia's first offshore oil exploration under a TPAO concession in April 2026, and the Blue Economy Ministry was inaugurated on April 23. The SNA's participation in international exercises in Turkey reflects an effort to build conventional military professionalism and interoperability alongside the ongoing counterinsurgency campaign against Al-Shabaab. However, critics — including opposition MPs in Somalia and Uganda's military chief Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who publicly questioned Turkey's expanding role in April — have raised concerns about the terms and scope of Ankara's growing strategic presence. The exercise occurs amid Somalia's constitutional crisis (11 days to President Mohamud's May 15 term expiry) and a worsening piracy surge that has elevated the maritime threat to 'severe.'

title: Somali Pirates Seize MT Eureka Diesel Tanker in Gulf of Aden — Third Major Hijacking in 10 Days
detail: Somali pirates seized the Togo-flagged product tanker MT Eureka (3,300 DWT, owned by Royal Shipping Lines/UAE) on May 2, 2026, hijacking the vessel near Qana port off Yemen's Shabwa province coast in the Gulf of Aden. Approximately nine armed gunmen stormed the tanker, which was carrying approximately 2,800 tons of diesel fuel, and redirected it across the Gulf of Aden toward the northeastern coast of Somalia. The vessel's crew of 12 — including Egyptian and Indian nationals — is now under pirate control. Yemen's coast guard launched recovery efforts and alerted international maritime partners, but the MT Eureka had cleared Yemeni waters by the time response assets were deployed. The MT Eureka seizure marks the third major piracy incident off Somalia in 10 days, after the Honour 25 (April 25, 17 crew including 10 Pakistanis) and the Sward general cargo vessel (April 27, 15 crew). At least four vessels have now been hijacked in the region since mid-April. Intelligence analysts have noted a possible coordination dimension between Houthi militia networks and Somali pirate groups — consistent with the UN Monitoring Group's 2024 documentation of an Al-Shabaab–Houthi weapons-for-piracy arrangement. EU NAVFOR Atalanta formally attributed the piracy resurgence to the Iran War redirecting counter-piracy naval assets to the Persian Gulf. The Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) elevated the piracy threat level to 'severe' on May 1. The MT Eureka's diesel cargo was destined for civilian use; its seizure compounds fuel supply disruptions that have already tripled gas prices in Mogadishu in 2026.

media.caption: Togo-flagged product tanker MT Eureka seized by Somali pirates near Yemen's Shabwa coast on May 2, 2026 — 12 crew held, vessel diverted to Somalia
